sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the term "small thing" for the debates of Abaye and Rava stems from the Torah being clothed in small matters, and this description applies to the Torah itself relative to its inner dimension and the Ein Sof clothed within it.

translations.translation: And it may be said that according to the reason that the debates of Abaye and Rava are called a small thing because the Torah was clothed in small matters,
the description "small thing" is from the perspective of the garments of the Torah.
Therefore he adds that the Torah of the present is a small thing relative to the inner dimension of the Torah that will be revealed in the future,
[and also that it is a small thing relative to the Ein Sof clothed within it],
for according to this reason,
the description "small thing" is
(also)
with regard to the Torah itself.
[And that he also brings the first reason—that the Torah was clothed in small matters—
it may be said,
for in this reason it is emphasized that the difference between the debates of Abaye and Rava and the Account of the Chariot is a difference from one extreme to the other,
as above].

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section further explains that the Torah is called a "small thing" due to the extreme self-nullification of the halachah relative to the Ein Sof clothed within it, and raises a question about why the Chariot, which is also nullified to its Rider, is called a "great thing."

translations.translation: And he continues in the maamar with further explanation that the Torah is called a small thing,
which is because of the extreme self-nullification of the halachah relative to the Ein Sof clothed within it.
For just as a person's study of Torah must be with self-nullification,
"My tongue shall answer Your word"50,
like one who answers after the reader51,
so too is it with regard to the halachos of the Torah themselves, that they are in a state of self-nullification to the Ein Sof clothed within them,
as will be explained below.
[And it may be said,
that according to the interpretation of "small" in its simple sense,
the description "small thing" is in relation to other matters.
But according to the interpretation that "small" denotes self-nullification
[like "I am small from all the kindnesses"52],
the smallness
(self-nullification)
is in it itself].
And it must be understood
(according to the interpretation that "small" denotes self-nullification),
behold, even the Chariot is in a state of self-nullification to the Rider,
and nevertheless it is called a great thing.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the self-nullification called "small thing" is total nullification with no merit, unlike the Chariot which has existence and advantage, while the halachos clothed in physical matters are utterly nullified, thereby drawing nullification to the person studying them.

translations.translation: And the point of the explanation may be said,
that the self-nullification which is called by the name "small thing"
("I am small"),
is
that it is utterly nullified and has no virtue whatsoever.
And as it is written in Igeres HaKodesh regarding "I am small"53,
that one makes himself like actual refuse and waste that has no need whatsoever.
And since the Chariot has existence,
to the extent that it has an advantage over the Rider
[and as above, that through the Chariot the Rider can reach a place that He cannot reach on His own],
therefore it is not a small thing.
[And on the contrary, because of the elevation within it,
through which it ascends to the aspect of "great"
(Arich),
the Chariot is also called a great thing].
And the halachos of the Torah that are clothed in physical matters
[the first interpretation of "small thing"],
since physical matters have no value54
relative to His wisdom and will, blessed be He, that are clothed within them,
behold they are in the ultimate state of self-nullification,
a small thing.
And through the self-nullification within the halachos of the Torah themselves,
self-nullification is also drawn into the person who engages in Torah,
so that his Torah study will be in the manner of "my tongue shall answer Your word,"
like one who answers after the reader.
